subject: Meadow Glen Mall Wegmans Extended Hours
overview: The Council approved a special permit for extended hours at a new Wegmans supermarket following negotiations over noise mitigation and authorized over $300,000 in funding for school energy efficiency grants. It also addressed infrastructure concerns regarding city-wide road paving and the establishment of a new historic district.

items.title: Special Permit: Ultimate Tango
items.summary: Approved a special permit for extended operating hours at 5 High Street.

items.title: Public Hearing: Comcast Conduit Installation
items.summary: Approved a petition for conduit and vault installation on Ashland and Salem Streets for Century Bank, conditioned on curb-to-curb paving and night work to mitigate traffic.

items.title: Comcast Conduit (Item 17-593)
items.summary: Approved the conduit project for High Street and Hillside Avenue with the same curb-to-curb paving and scheduling requirements as the previous Comcast project.

items.title: Payment of Prior Year Invoices
items.summary: Approved the payment of $4,362.25 for fire station door repairs and $545 for emergency residential plumbing and heating repairs from prior fiscal years.

items.title: Energy Efficiency Grants and Free Cash Appropriation
items.summary: Approved an appropriation of $348,336 to provide matching funds for state grants to upgrade lighting at Andrews School and install battery storage at both the school and the DPW facility.

items.title: Evans Street Road Maintenance
items.summary: Referred a resident's complaint regarding the lack of road maintenance on Evans Street to the administration for an update on the status of planned paving and utility work.

items.title: Special Permit: Wegmans Extended Hours
items.summary: Approved an extension of operating hours for the Wegmans at Meadow Glen Mall to 6:00 AM to midnight for the store and 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM for deliveries, with mandatory reviews at 30, 60, and 90 days. The permit includes conditions for noise mitigation, including a ban on overnight trash pickup and a requirement for sealed loading docks.

items.title: Subcommittee on Business and Economic Development Report
items.summary: Adopted the committee report and approved a sign permit for the Evangelical Haitian Church with restrictions on illumination and message frequency.

items.title: Resolutions: Hegner Center, Tree Fungus, and Traffic Engineer
items.summary: Approved resolutions requesting updates on a tree fungus infestation, future plans for the Hegner Center, and the status of hiring a municipal traffic engineer.

items.title: Resolutions: Historic Districts and Airplane Noise
items.summary: Requested that the Historic District Commission analyze a proposed Medford Square Historic District and called for a citywide reverse 911 alert to coordinate resident noise complaints to the FAA.

items.title: Flashing Stop Signs Pilot Program
items.summary: Referred a proposal for a 10-intersection pilot program using flashing stop signs to the administration for pricing and the Traffic Commission for location review.

items.title: TV3/Medford Community Media Operations
items.summary: Discussed the criteria for local access membership and broadcasting, including the city's requirement for CORI checks for producers using the high school studio.

items.title: Superintendent Update on Enrollment and Development
items.summary: Superintendent Roy Belson addressed the Council to dispute claims that new real estate developments are overrunning school capacity, stating that average elementary class sizes remain around 18 students.
